There is no running Worker, no account, and the corpus is fixtures. Taking it now costs nothing; after the first deploy it is precisely the hard case the split exists for. ## The gate judged it `0007` declares `-- contract-of: utterances` against `0002`'s `-- expand: utterances`. I checked the gate was really judging and not just passing: pointing the marker at a name nothing declares turns it red on *"a contract step retires an expand that an earlier migration declared"*. That is the mechanism from #41 doing exactly the job it was built for, on the first migration that ever needed it. ## Six leaves retire, three are reworded A leaf only retires if a leaf about the new shape already carries its guarantee: | retired | carried now by | |---|---| | `1.2` a statement keeps its id on re-extraction | `3.9` a replay writes nothing new | | `1.5` re-analysis supersedes a judgment | `1.12` re-analysis supersedes a finding | | `4.2` / `4.3` the two judgment kinds | `4.7` / `4.8` anomaly and trend change | | `4.4` / `4.5` consistent pairs kept, judgment trail | `1.11` / `1.12` / `1.13` | Three had **no sibling**, so they were reworded rather than dropped — this is the part I'd have got wrong by deleting section 4 wholesale: - `1.3` and `1.6` move to utterances. The "unknown is its own state" rule and ULID monotonicity are as true of utterances as they were of statements. - `4.1` becomes what pairing was actually protecting. The old leaf was about drawing candidate pairs from one figure's statements; the guarantee underneath it is that **two people disagreeing is public life, not an inconsistency**. Its case now puts two personas in one subject at opposite ends of the axis and proves neither produces a finding. ## Detection had nothing calling it #50 landed the maths and its proof; nothing invoked it. It now runs at the end of the scheduled pass, per persona and per subject, at the same model and prompt the placements were made under — a series that mixed two would be measuring the models against each other rather than the persona. ## Two things that fell out **The harness stopped rewriting `wrangler.toml`.** That file existed only to strip the `[ai]` binding, which made wrangler open an authenticated remote proxy and refuse to start without a token. Its own drift guard caught the removal and said, in its error message, "the subtraction is no longer needed (delete it)". So the harness now runs the *committed* config — no gap at all between what the tests run and what deploys. **One of #28's honest gaps is moot rather than deferred.** "The judge model is unevaluated for Hebrew" — there is no judge model. Detection is pure code over a stance series. The banner now says what is actually true: no embedding or stance model has been *chosen* yet, which is #27's. ## Folders touched
**`src/backend/corpus/`** — `0007` drops `judgments`, `statements_fts`, `statements`. `store.ts` loses the statement and judgment mappers, types and every method over them. **`src/backend/`** — `analysis/` is gone entirely. `index.ts` loses the queue consumer and gains the detection pass. `env.ts` binds `CORPUS`, `RAW` and one var; the `Queue`, `MessageBatch` and `Ai` types go with what used them. **`src/backend/acquisition/`** — `extractInto` writes utterances only; `ModuleOutcome` loses its statement count. **`src/shared/`** — `Statement`, `Judgment`, `JudgmentKind`, `SURFACED_KINDS` and every wire type over them. **(root)** — `wrangler.toml` loses the queue producer, the queue consumer, `[ai]` and `JUDGE_MODEL`. `wrangler deploy --dry-run` now resolves three bindings instead of six.
